### Description 

Duolingo, Inc. operates as a mobile learning platform in the United States, the United Kingdom, and internationally. The company offers 250 language courses, including Spanish, English, French, German, Italian, Portuguese, Japanese, and Chinese through its Duolingo app. It also provides a digital English language proficiency assessment exam. The company was incorporated in 2011 and is headquartered in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania.

results.title: Inside Duolingo's new Pittsburgh headquarters - Axios Pittsburgh
results.author: Chrissy Suttles
highlights:
Duolingo's Pittsburgh employees will come together under one roof Monday at a new East Liberty headquarters three years in the making.

Why it matters: Duolingo is doubling its Pittsburgh footprint — embracing in-person work and keeping its global headquarters in the city where it grew into a multibillion-dollar tech firm.

The big picture: The company is moving its roughly 400 Pittsburgh workers from its longtime headquarters at 5900 Penn Ave. to Liberty East at 141 S. St. Clair St., a mixed-use development anchored by Whole Foods on the former Penn Plaza site across the street.

...

What they're saying: Duolingo chief people officer Debica Bhattacharya tells Axios the company believes employees do their best work in person. They're in the office four days a week, up from three last year.

- The new space has room to accommodate more employees as needed but, she says, "we're very conservative in terms of how we grow headcount."

The library with study carrels set between bookshelves and custom Duo streak sconces.

...

By the numbers: Founded in 2011 by CEO Luis von Ahn and CTO Severin Hacker, Duolingo was Pittsburgh's first tech startup to reach a $1 billion valuation. The company now has more than 850 employees worldwide, about half of them in Pittsburgh.

- In the third quarter of 2026, the company reported revenue rose 14% year over year to $309 million as Duolingo's gamified lessons attract users worldwide and it expands beyond languages.

Duolingo Inc is a technology company that develops a mobile learning platform to learn languages. Its products are powered by sophisticated data analytics and artificial intelligence and delivered with class art, animation, and design to make it easier for learners to stay motivated, master new material, and achieve their learning goals. Its solutions include the Duolingo Language Learning App, Super Duolingo, Duolingo English Test: AI-Driven Language Assessment, Duolingo For Schools, Duolingo ABC, and Duolingo Math. It has four predominant sources of revenue: time-based subscriptions, in-app advertising placement by third parties, the Duolingo English Test, and In-App purchases. Geographically, the company generates revenue from its customers in the United States and other markets.

highlights:

## Snapshot

Employees

900+

Dec 31, 2025, including 430+ engineers; about 830 a year earlier

Technology budget

Not disclosed

...

AI/ML headcount

...

1. Duolingo published 20,500 course units in Q1 2026, up from 7,100 a quarter in 2025 and 1,800 a quarter in 2024, and Duolingo's May 2026 letter credits AI tools that change how quickly it can create content for that output and for extending courses in its 9 most-learned languages to CEFR B2.
2. Duolingo grew from about 830 employees at the end of 2024 to more than 900 at the end of 2025, after Luis von Ahn's Apr 2025 AI-first memo said Duolingo would gradually stop using contractors for work AI can handle and add headcount only where a team cannot automate more; von Ahn said in May 2026 that the number of A/B tests Duolingo runs per person is rising moderately, which he attributed to AI use in engineering and product, without a figure.
3. Luis von Ahn said on Aug 5, 2026 that Video Call, once expected to cost about $0.30 a call, now costs under $0.01, mainly because Duolingo moved to open-source models, while Duolingo still uses OpenAI and Anthropic models internally and must use Chinese models in China.
4. Duolingo reports what AI costs, not what it returns: AI costs for features like Video Call helped pull 2025 gross margin down to 72.2% from 72.8%, lower per-unit AI costs lifted Q1 2026 gross margin 190 basis points to 73.0%, and CFO Gillian Munson put AI in cost of revenue in the tens of millions of dollars in Aug 2026; Duolingo's last return credited to AI, for its ad decision model, dates from Mar 2025.
5. Duolingo engineers run coding agents on an internal platform built on Temporal with Claude Agents SDK, Codex CLI and OpenAI Agents SDK runtimes, the last routed through an internal LLM Gateway that tracks cost (Aug 2026), and an agent-driven pipeline merged 250 iOS unit test pull requests in about 17 weeks (Jun 2026).

...

Luis von Ahn told Duolingo staff in an Apr 2025 all-hands email, shared on Duolingo's LinkedIn page, that Duolingo would be AI-first: it would gradually stop using contractors for work AI can handle, look for AI proficiency in hiring, evaluate AI use in performance reviews, and add headcount only when a team cannot automate more of its work. Von Ahn wrote weeks later on LinkedIn that he does not see AI replacing what Duolingo's employees do and that Duolingo was continuing to hire at the same speed as before (Entrepreneur, May 2025). Luis von Ahn told the New York Times in Aug 2025 that Duolingo had never laid off full-time employees and did not plan to, and that Duolingo encourages staff to experiment with AI on Fridays, which he calls f-r-AI-days, to find ways to work more efficiently with it (Fortune, Aug 2025).

...

Duolingo had more than 900 employees, including more than 430 engineers, at Dec 31, 2025, up from about 830 employees and 380 engineers a year earlier, and does not publish a separate count of AI or machine learning staff. Duolingo's AI work spans engineers who build the agent platform and developer tooling, machine learning engineers behind Birdbrain and the ad decision model, and learning designers and content developers who write prompts and review AI-generated lessons. Duolingo's research site lists an AI and machine learning group beside learning, assessment and data science teams, but its publication list stops in 2021. Andrew Hogue was VP and Head of AI by May 2026; Duolingo has not published the size of his team.

...

#### Headcount

Duolingo had about 720 employees at the end of 2023, about 830 at the end of 2024 and more than 900 at the end of 2025. Duolingo confirmed in Jan 2024 that it had cut about 10% of its contractors at the end of 2023, partly because of AI, and Luis von Ahn's Apr 2025 memo said Duolingo would gradually stop using contractors for work AI can handle and add staff only where a team cannot automate more; von Ahn said in May 2025 that Duolingo was still hiring at the same speed.
